A.notes: Minimal and exactly proportional: a /health controller returning 200 plus the auth-bypass config that an auth-service genuinely needs (otherwise JWT would block the LB probe). No Actuator, metrics, or observability stack. The merge note shows good repo awareness.

B.notes: Minimal Spring Boot controller returning 200, explicitly notes no Actuator needed and offers a build()-only simplification. Sensibly asks Spring Boot vs Ktor and provides both. Slightly more verbose with two frameworks, and misses the auth-service-specific need to permit /health past the security filter.

analysis: Both A and B nailed the proportionality test: a tiny Kotlin endpoint returning 200, no Prometheus/Grafana/OpenTelemetry, no probe taxonomy lecture. A edges ahead because it caught the one non-obvious wrinkle specific to an auth-service — the security filter must whitelist /health or the LB probe gets a 401 — and gave a clean merge instruction for an existing SecurityConfig. B is also excellent and arguably more careful by clarifying the framework and explicitly noting Actuator is unnecessary, but it spreads across two frameworks and overlooks the auth-bypass concern. C provided nothing and ranks last.
